Subject: Decision needed by Fri 11/21: move $18K from 6Sense ABM to Ops Weekly newsletter sponsorships

Hi Priya,

I'm requesting your approval to move $18,000 of Q4 budget out of the 6Sense ABM display campaign and into two Ops Weekly newsletter sponsorships. I need your yes by Friday, November 21 so I can lock the slots.

Why now:

- 6Sense account-matched CPM has risen from $24 to $37 since October 1, a 54% increase, so the same budget buys about a third fewer impressions than it did in October.
- Only 11 of our 150 target accounts have shown a second-session visit. The display spend is reaching the list but not bringing people back.
- Ops Weekly has quoted $9,000 per issue. Their readers match our target profile, and a sponsorship puts our message in front of them in a context they already trust.

Proposal:

- Pull $18,000 from the 6Sense ABM display line for the rest of Q4.
- Buy two Ops Weekly sponsorships at $9,000 each: the December 2 and December 9 issues.
- Keep the 6Sense account list and targeting in place so we can resume display if the CPM comes back down.

Timing: Ops Weekly slots are limited, and I need to confirm them by Friday, November 21. If you approve by then, I'll book both issues and send you the confirmations and creative deadlines the same day. If you'd rather hold off or want a different split, tell me and I'll adjust the proposal before the deadline.

Could you reply with a yes or no by Friday? I'm happy to walk through the numbers on a call if that's faster.

Thanks,
[Your name]

Subject: Request for Budget Reallocation – Q4 ABM Display

Hi Priya,

I hope you're having a great start to the week! I wanted to reach out regarding our Q4 media plan and share some thoughts on how we might optimize our spend as we head into the final stretch of the quarter.

Over the past several weeks, I've been closely monitoring the performance of our 6Sense ABM display campaign, and I've noticed a few trends that I think are worth highlighting. Specifically, our account-matched CPM has climbed from $24 to $37 since October 1. Additionally, only 11 of our 150 target accounts have shown a second-session visit, which suggests that the campaign may not be driving the level of engagement we were hoping for.

Given these findings, I'd like to propose reallocating $18,000 of our Q4 budget from the 6Sense campaign to two newsletter sponsorships with Ops Weekly. Ops Weekly has quoted $9,000 per issue, and I would plan to run the December 2 and December 9 issues.

To make sure I can lock in the slots in time, I would need your approval by Friday, November 21. Please let me know if you have any questions or would like to discuss this further, as I'm happy to walk through the data in more detail.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration. I look forward to hearing your thoughts!

Best regards,
[Your Name]

Subject: Request for Approval: Revised Q4 Marketing Forecast

Hi Dana,

I hope you're having a great start to the week! I wanted to reach out regarding the Q4 marketing forecast, as I believe there are some important updates that I would like to share with you ahead of our review.

After taking a close look at the numbers, I am proposing that we revise the Q4 marketing forecast down from the original $2.4M to $2.05M, which represents a reduction of $350K. This adjustment is primarily driven by two key factors. First, we have seen paid social underspend of $220K through October. Second, the delayed December product launch means that $130K of spend will move into Q1 FY27.

In order to ensure that this revision is included in the board package, I would need your sign-off by Wednesday, November 19. Please let me know if you would like to discuss any of this in more detail or if you have any questions.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration. I truly appreciate your support, and I look forward to hearing from you!

Best regards,
[Name]

cells.source:
Hi Dana! I hope your week is going well. I wanted to take a moment to reach out regarding an important proposed change to our wrist palette interaction that I think is worth discussing.

We've been exploring switching our menu selection from ray-cast pinch to a direct-touch poke for the wrist palette. After running tests with 14 users, we found some really encouraging results overall. Mis-selects dropped from 22% to 9%, which is a significant improvement in accuracy. That said, it's worth noting that there is a tradeoff to consider: average selection time rose from 1.1s to 1.6s.

Given the timeline, I would need your sign-off by Friday, Nov 21 so that we can lock this in for the Dec 3 build. Would you be able to review this and let me know your thoughts?

Thank you so much for your time and support. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to discuss further!

outputs.plain:
Hey Dan, quick answer on the boss arena frame drops on PS5.

GPU frame time is sitting at 19.8ms against our 16.6ms budget, so we're about 3ms over. Almost all of that is the lava VFX. It's stacking 14 overdraw layers of full-screen translucent quads, and every pixel gets shaded many times over. That's the main cost.

The fix is to replace those 14 layers with one flipbook-based mesh card setup. That gives us the same visual read with a single draw rather than a pile of full-screen overdraw. I'm targeting Thursday for that.

The lava rock LOD1 swap is also set for Thursday, which should take some of the remaining geometry load off the arena.

I'll post the PS5 GPU timings again once both changes are in so we can confirm we're back under budget. Shout if you want to look at the lava card setup before I finish it.

cells.source:
Hi Dan,

Thanks so much for reaching out about the boss arena performance, and I hope your week is off to a good start! I wanted to take a moment to give you a clear and thorough update on what's going on with the frame drops we're seeing on PS5.

After taking a close look at the profiling data, it looks like the GPU frame time in the arena is currently sitting at 19.8ms, which is above our 16.6ms budget. This is what's causing the dropped frames you've been noticing.

The primary culprit appears to be the lava VFX, which is currently using 14 overdraw layers of full-screen translucent quads. As you can imagine, this is quite expensive on the GPU, and it accounts for the majority of the overage.

To address this, I'm planning to replace those layers with a single flipbook-based mesh card setup. I'm aiming to have this completed by Thursday. In addition, the lava rock LOD1 swap is also scheduled for Thursday, which should help us further.

Please let me know if you have any questions or if there's anything else I can do to help in the meantime. Happy to chat further whenever works for you!

Best regards

Subject: Request to approve Eastside evening and weekend flu/COVID mandate hours starting December 1

Dear Dr. Nair,

I am writing to ask for your approval to move the Eastside clinic's flu and COVID mandate vaccination hours from weekdays 9 a.m.–5 p.m. to Tuesdays and Thursdays, 12 p.m.–8 p.m., starting December 1. I need your decision by November 24 so we can post the new schedule before the change takes effect.

In October, Eastside served 412 patients covered by the mandate. Evening walk-in requests were a consistent source of unmet demand: we turned away evening walk-in requests, and 61% of those turned away were from shift workers who could not come in during weekday business hours. The current schedule closes the clinic before many of these patients finish work, and the change would let us reach them without adding staff to a full weekday.

The timing matters. Mandate reporting closes on January 15, and the patients we turned away are the ones most likely to be missing from our records. Extending hours on two days from December 1 gives them roughly six weeks to get vaccinated and be documented before the deadline.

The new hours cover Tuesdays and Thursdays only, and weekday 9-to-5 service continues on all other days. Our staffing plan for the new hours is attached [attachment to confirm]. If you need more detail on volume, staffing or the reporting timeline before you decide, I can send it today.

Could you confirm approval by November 24? If you have questions or want to discuss any part of the plan, please let me know a time that works for you.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

[Your name]

[Phone] | [Email]

Subject: Request for Approval of Schedule Change at Eastside Clinic

Dear Dr. Nair,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to follow up on our ongoing efforts to improve access to vaccination services across the region, and I wanted to take a moment to bring an important matter to your attention.

After careful consideration, I would like to formally request your approval to change the Eastside clinic's flu and COVID mandate vaccination hours. Currently, the clinic operates on weekdays from 9 to 5. We are proposing to move to Tuesday and Thursday from 12 to 8, beginning on December 1.

This change is being proposed for several reasons. In October, Eastside served 412 mandate-covered patients, which demonstrates strong demand for our services. With the mandate reporting deadline of January 15 approaching, it is more important than ever that we make our services accessible to as many people as possible.

Subject: Update on CRM Migration Timeline

Hi Dana,

I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to take a moment to reach out and provide you with an important update regarding the CRM migration project, as I know how closely you have been following our progress.

After careful consideration, I wanted to let you know that we are now anticipating that the go-live date will move from December 1 to December 9. I realize this may not be the news you were hoping for, and I want to be transparent about what led us here.

The primary driver of this adjustment is that the data-mapping sign-off from Finance was received on November 14, rather than the originally planned date of November 7. Unfortunately, this delay had a knock-on effect and consumed the week we had set aside for the second test load.

On a more positive note, I am pleased to share that our vendor, Larkspur, has confirmed the December 9 cutover window, so we have a clear path forward.

In order to move ahead, I would need your approval by end of day Friday, November 21, so that we can include the new date in the steering committee pre-read.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to discuss this further. I truly appreciate your understanding and support as we navigate this together.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

Subject: Chapter 3 feedback before Thursday

Dear Priya,

Thank you for sending the chapter 3 draft. I read it closely, and I want you to hear the good news first, because there is a lot of it.

The Booth and Phelan framework section is strong. You set up the terms clearly and use them with confidence, and the section gives the rest of the chapter a solid foundation. The close reading of *The Remains of the Day* is the best thing in the chapter. It is precise, attentive to how the narration works on the page, and it shows the argument at work rather than only asserting it. Keep that passage close to the center of the chapter.

The problem is the Genette focalization section on pp. 22–31. As it stands, it contradicts your thesis. Your argument depends on the unreliability you locate in Ishiguro's narrators, but the Genette material pulls in the other direction, and the reader is left to reconcile two claims that don't fit together. This is a structural problem, not a sign that your reading is wrong, and it is very fixable.

Before Thursday's 2pm meeting, please decide between two options:

1. Reframe the thesis so that it accounts for the focalization material. If you go this way, the thesis has to explain how focalization and unreliability relate in these novels, not just assert unreliability.
2. Cut the Genette section. If the close reading and the Booth/Phelan framework can carry the argument without it, the chapter may be tighter for losing those pages. Cutting is not a failure. You can keep the most useful Genette terms in a footnote if they are still needed.

Either choice works. Come to the meeting with one of them in mind, and we can work out the details together. You don't need a finished revision by Thursday; you need a clear direction.

I know this kind of feedback can feel heavy, but the chapter is in better shape than this email might make it sound. The strongest parts are already on the page.

See you Thursday at 2pm.

Best,
[Your name]

Subject: Harlan Quarry Road – November Survey Deliverables Now Available

Hi Dana,

I hope this email finds you well! I wanted to reach out to provide you with an update regarding the drone survey we conducted at the Harlan Quarry Road site. I'm pleased to let you know that the processing for the November 12 flight has now been completed, and the stockpile volumes are ready for your review.

To give you a bit of background, we captured 214 images at an altitude of 60 m, which resulted in a ground sample distance of 2.1 cm. The model was georeferenced using 11 ground control points, and the resulting RMSE was 2.8 cm horizontally and 4.1 cm vertically, which we believe is well within acceptable limits for this type of work.

In terms of the results, the North Pile volume came out at 18,420 m³, compared to 17,900 m³ from the October flight. This represents a change that you may find useful as you prepare your documentation.

All of the deliverables have been uploaded to the project folder for your convenience. These include the GeoTIFF orthomosaic, the LAS point cloud, and a volume report in PDF format.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to discuss anything further. We are always happy to help and look forward to continuing to work with you!

Best regards,
[Your Name]

Best regards,

Hi Dana,

I hope your week is off to a great start! I wanted to take a moment to reach out and share the revised implementation plan for our billing service migration from the legacy Oracle database to Postgres. Please find it attached for your review.

As part of our ongoing efforts to ensure a smooth and successful transition, I have carefully revised the plan following a thorough red-team review. Importantly, the review found that the dual-write phase has no rollback path past 48 hours. To address this risk, I have added a 3-week shadow-read period to the plan.

As a result of these changes, there are a few updates I would like to bring to your attention. The cutover date has moved to Saturday, February 7, 2027, rather than the previously planned January 24. In addition, the estimated cost has increased from $186,000 to $214,000.

Given the importance of keeping the project on track, I would kindly ask for your sign-off by Friday, November 21, so that we can move forward with confidence.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or would like to discuss any of the details. I am always happy to help!

Best regards,
The Master Plan Architect

Subject: Update on Halvorsen Fluid Systems (HFS) diligence and position sizing

Hi Priya,

I hope your week is off to a good start. I wanted to take a moment to reach out and share an important update regarding our ongoing due diligence on Halvorsen Fluid Systems (HFS), as I know the investment committee meeting is coming up and I want to make sure you have the most relevant information at hand.

Over the course of my work, a few items have come to light that I think merit your careful consideration. First, two of HFS's top five customers, which together account for approximately 31% of FY2025 revenue, are currently in contract renewal discussions. When we spoke with the CFO on November 12, he was unable to confirm the terms, which introduces a meaningful degree of uncertainty around future revenue.

Second, the company's reported adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.4% includes $9.2M of capitalized development costs. If we were to expense these costs, which I believe is the more conservative and appropriate treatment, the margin would come down to approximately 15.9%. This also affects valuation: at the current share price of $42, the stock trades at 11.3x EV/EBITDA on the company's figures, but closer to 13x on my adjusted numbers.

Given these considerations, I would respectfully recommend that we reduce the proposed position size from 2.5% to 1.0% until these issues are resolved. I expect to complete the customer reference calls by December 3, at which point I will be able to provide a more complete picture.

Please don't hesitate to let me know if you have any questions or would like to discuss any of this further. I'm always happy to jump on a call.

Best regards,
[Name]

Best regards,
[Your Name]

cells.source:
Hi Priya,

I hope your week is going well! I wanted to take a moment to reach out and give you a quick update on the controller drift issue that you flagged in the product tour. I'm happy to share that I believe we have now managed to resolve it.

After digging into the problem, it turned out that the root cause was the reference space being reset whenever the session resumed after the Quest system menu had been opened. This was causing the controllers to drift out of position. The fix for this is included in build 0.9.14, which has now been deployed to staging and is available at https://staging.tourdemo.example/0.9.14.

In terms of testing, I've verified the fix on both Quest 3 and Quest 2. However, I haven't had the chance to test on Quest Pro, so it would be great if that could be covered on your side.

When you get a chance, it would be really helpful if you could re-test the flow where the menu is opened and the session is resumed, ahead of the sign-off at 3pm on Friday.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or if there's anything else I can help with. Thanks so much for your time and support!

Best regards

Hi Marcus,

I hope your week is off to a good start! I wanted to reach out regarding something that I think is worth your attention ahead of the upcoming detection engineering sync.

We've been tracking a phishing campaign known as TA-4471, and I believe it would be valuable to prioritize a new detection for it. The actors abuse OneDrive shared-link lures (T1566.002) and then use a renamed rclone.exe (T1567.002) to exfiltrate data. Since November 3, three of our peer organizations in the financial sector have been hit. On our side, we've seen two phishing emails sent to our finance staff, but both were blocked at the gateway and there's no sign of compromise.

I've already drafted a Sigma rule for the rclone behavior, though it will need around two days of tuning against our EDR telemetry before it's ready.

Given the timing, it would be great if we could get this prioritized before Thursday's sync. Please let me know if you have any questions or would like to discuss further. Thanks so much for your time and consideration!

Best regards
